# Start a New Project: CMS Statement of Deficiency Extraction & AI Plan of Action
I want to build a local-hosted MVP application that processes CMS (Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services) survey documents.

The application should allow a user to upload a CMS document, extract the Provider/Supplier (Medicare Center) Name, CMS Tag/ID, and Statement of Deficiency (SOD), and then use an AI layer to generate a draft Plan of Action / Plan of Correction for each extracted SOD.

This project is starting from scratch.

## 1. Core Business Problem
CMS survey documents can contain one or more Statements of Deficiency. Identifying the relevant deficiencies, CMS tags, and provider information from these documents can require significant manual effort.

The application should reduce this manual effort by:

1. Accepting an uploaded CMS document.
2. Extracting structured information from the document.
3. Identifying each Statement of Deficiency and its associated CMS Tag.
4. Identifying the Provider/Supplier or Medicare Center Name.
5. Generating an AI-assisted draft Plan of Action for each SOD.
6. Presenting the extracted information and generated plans to a human for review and editing.
The AI output is assistance only. The application must not automatically submit anything to CMS or represent the generated plan as an approved regulatory response.

---

# 2. MVP Scope
The initial MVP should focus on two primary layers.

## Layer 1 â€” CMS Document Extraction
The application must support CMS documents that may be:

- Digitally generated PDFs
- Text-based PDFs
- Scanned PDFs
- Image-based documents
- Documents containing a mixture of digital text and scanned pages
The extraction layer should intelligently determine how to process the uploaded document.

Conceptual pipeline:

Uploaded CMS Document
â†’ File Validation
â†’ Document Analysis
â†’ Native Text Extraction
â†’ OCR fallback when required
â†’ Text Normalization
â†’ CMS Structure Detection
â†’ Provider/Supplier Extraction
â†’ CMS Tag Extraction
â†’ SOD Extraction
â†’ Structured Extraction Result

The extraction layer should be designed for accuracy and traceability.

For each extracted value, where practical, retain:

- Extracted value
- Source page
- Relevant source text/snippet
- Confidence/uncertainty information
The system must support multiple SODs in a single document.

Example:

Provider/Supplier:
ABC Medicare Center

Deficiencies:

SOD 1

- Tag: F880
- Statement of Deficiency: ...
- Source Page: 4
SOD 2

- Tag: F689
- Statement of Deficiency: ...
- Source Page: 7
SOD 3

- Tag: F656
- Statement of Deficiency: ...
- Source Page: 10
Do not assume that every CMS document has identical formatting. The extraction design should account for reasonable variations in document structure and formatting.

---

# 3. Layer 2 â€” AI Plan of Action
Each extracted SOD should be independently passed to an AI layer.

Conceptual flow:

Extracted SOD
+
CMS Tag
+
Relevant available context
â†“
AI Processing
â†“
Draft Plan of Action / Plan of Correction

The generated plan must be grounded in the extracted SOD.

The AI must NOT fabricate:

- Residents
- Staff
- Incidents
- Policies
- Dates
- Actions already performed
- Facility-specific facts
- Compliance status
- Other information that is not supported by the available input
If required information is missing, the system should identify the missing information rather than inventing it.

The generated output must clearly be identified as AI-generated draft content.

The user must be able to review and edit it.

---

# 4. Human-in-the-Loop Workflow
The application should follow this workflow:

Upload CMS Document
â†“
Extract Document
â†“
Display Provider + Tags + SODs
â†“
Human Reviews Extraction
â†“
Generate AI Plan of Action
â†“
Display AI Draft
â†“
Human Reviews/Edits
â†“
Human Approves

The system must distinguish between:

- Extracted content
- AI-generated content
- User-edited content
- User-approved content
No automatic CMS submission or external regulatory communication is required.

---

# 5. Localhost Requirement
This is a local MVP.

The application must run entirely on localhost during the initial development phase.

Do not introduce cloud deployment at this stage.

Do not introduce database integration.

Application state should remain in memory for now.

The conceptual architecture is:

Frontend
â†“
Backend/API
â†“
Extraction Layer
â†“
AI Layer
â†“
In-Memory Application State

A database should NOT be added to the MVP.

However, design the application with reasonable separation of concerns so that persistent storage can be introduced later without redesigning the entire application.

---

# 6. Suggested System Components
The architecture should be modular.

At minimum, evaluate the need for:

### Frontend
Responsible for:

- Uploading documents
- Showing processing status
- Displaying provider information
- Displaying extracted SODs
- Displaying CMS Tags
- Showing source/page information
- Triggering AI generation
- Displaying generated Plans of Action
- Allowing users to edit generated plans
- Showing AI-generated vs user-edited content

### Backend/API
Responsible for:

- File upload
- Validation
- Workflow orchestration
- Extraction orchestration
- AI orchestration
- In-memory state management
- API responses
- Error handling

### Extraction Service
Responsible for:

- Digital text extraction
- OCR
- Text normalization
- Document/page processing
- Provider extraction
- CMS Tag extraction
- SOD extraction
- Confidence/uncertainty
- Source references

### AI Service
Responsible for:

- Prompt construction
- LLM invocation
- SOD-specific Plan of Action generation
- Structured AI output
- AI error handling
Keep the extraction and AI layers independent so they can be tested separately.

---

# 7. Important Extraction Requirement
Extraction quality is a critical part of this project.

Do not treat OCR as an afterthought.

The system should support both:

1. Native text extraction when the document contains machine-readable text.
2. OCR when the document is scanned/image-based.
The architecture should allow different extraction mechanisms to be evaluated or replaced later.

The extraction process should also make it possible to trace an extracted SOD back to its source page/text.

If extraction confidence is low or a required field cannot be reliably identified, the UI should indicate that instead of silently returning an incorrect value.

---

# 8. Required Initial UI
The initial UI should be simple and focused.

### Upload Screen
CMS Document Processing

[Upload CMS Document]

Supported document types should be clearly communicated.

### Extraction Results
Show:

Provider/Supplier Name

Number of deficiencies identified

For each deficiency:

- CMS Tag
- Statement of Deficiency
- Source page
- Confidence/uncertainty
- Generate Plan of Action button

### Plan of Action
For each SOD:

- CMS Tag
- Statement of Deficiency
- AI-generated Plan of Action
- Edit capability
- Approval capability
The UI should prioritize clarity, traceability, and human review over visual complexity.

---

# 9. Privacy and Security
Even though this is a localhost MVP, uploaded CMS documents may contain sensitive information.

Therefore:

- Do not expose uploaded documents publicly.
- Do not persist documents in a database.
- Avoid logging full document contents.
- Do not log sensitive information unnecessarily.
- API keys must be stored using environment variables.
- Never hardcode API keys.
- Validate uploaded files.
- Apply reasonable file-size limits.
- Clearly identify when document content is sent to an external OCR or LLM service.
